--- title: "Advanced Features" description: "Incremental insertion, entity linking, temporal extraction, community reports, and graph rebuild — production features for real-world usage." date: today format: html: self-contained: true embed-resources: true code-fold: true code-tools: true --- ## Introduction nano-graphrag includes several advanced features for production use cases: - **Incremental insertion** — add new documents without reprocessing existing ones - **Entity linking** — merge duplicate entities across documents using LLM disambiguation - **Temporal extraction** — extract time-bound relationships (valid_from / valid_to) - **Community reports** — configure how community summaries are generated - **Graph rebuild** — reconstruct the knowledge graph from stored manifests This notebook demonstrates each feature with configuration examples. ## Setup ::: {#setup .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import logging import time from pathlib import Path logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING) logging.getLogger("nano-graphrag").setLevel(logging.INFO) TEXT_PART1 = ( "Alice is a quantum physicist at MIT. She published groundbreaking research on " "quantum entanglement in 2023. Her colleague Bob is a computer scientist working " "on quantum algorithms." ) TEXT_PART2 = ( "Alice Chen, the physicist from MIT, collaborated with Carol on a new paper about " "quantum error correction. Bob Smith also contributed to the project. Dave is their " "department head at MIT." ) ``` ::: ::: {#imports .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} from nano_graphrag import GraphRAG, QueryParam ``` ::: ## 1. Incremental Document Insertion `ainsert_documents()` accepts a dictionary of `{doc_id: text}` pairs. When you call it again with new documents, only the new ones are processed — existing documents (matched by content hash) are skipped. This is the recommended API for production workflows where documents arrive over time. ::: {#incremental-init .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} WORKING_DIR_INC = Path("./_cache/06_advanced_features/incremental") WORKING_DIR_INC.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) rag_inc = GraphRAG( working_dir=str(WORKING_DIR_INC), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}

If you insert the same text again, it's a no-op. The `document_index` KV store tracks which documents have been processed and their extraction manifests. You can also use `force_rebuild=True` to reprocess all documents: ::: {#force-rebuild-note .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} print("Force rebuild example (not executed to save API calls):") print() print(" await rag_inc.ainsert_documents(") print(" {'doc-3': 'New document text'},") print(" force_rebuild=True, # Reprocesses ALL docs") print(" )") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Force rebuild example (not executed to save API calls): await rag_inc.ainsert_documents( {'doc-3': 'New document text'}, force_rebuild=True, # Reprocesses ALL docs ) ``` ::: ::: ## 2. Entity Linking When `enable_entity_linking=True`, nano-graphrag uses a multi-step process to merge entities that refer to the same real-world thing: 1. **Exact match** — same name after normalization 2. **Fuzzy match** — similarity above `entity_linking_similarity_threshold` (default: 0.92) 3. **Neighborhood evidence** — overlapping graph neighbors (IoU above `entity_linking_iou_threshold`, default: 0.3) 4. **LLM disambiguation** — the LLM decides if ambiguous candidates are the same entity ::: {#entity-linking-config .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} WORKING_DIR_EL = Path("./_cache/06_advanced_features/entity_linking") WORKING_DIR_EL.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) rag_el = GraphRAG( working_dir=str(WORKING_DIR_EL), enable_entity_linking=True, entity_linking_similarity_threshold=0.85, entity_linking_max_candidates=3, entity_linking_iou_threshold=0.3, entity_linking_min_common_neighbors=2, ) print(f"Entity linking enabled: {rag_el.enable_entity_linking}") print(f"Similarity threshold: {rag_el.entity_linking_similarity_threshold}") print(f"Max candidates: {rag_el.entity_linking_max_candidates}") print(f"IoU threshold: {rag_el.entity_linking_iou_threshold}") print(f"Min common neighbors: {rag_el.entity_linking_min_common_neighbors}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}

This produces a more coherent knowledge graph when documents use different names for the same entities. Entity linking configuration reference: | Parameter | Default | Purpose | |-----------|---------|---------| | `entity_linking_similarity_threshold` | 0.92 | Minimum embedding similarity for fuzzy matching | | `entity_linking_max_candidates` | 3 | Max candidates to consider per entity | | `entity_linking_iou_threshold` | 0.3 | Min graph-neighborhood overlap for merge | | `entity_linking_min_common_neighbors` | 2 | Min shared neighbors for neighborhood evidence | | `entity_linking_use_neighborhood_evidence` | True | Use graph structure to validate merges | ## 3. Temporal Extraction When `enable_temporal_extraction=True`, the extraction pipeline adds temporal fields to relationships: - `temporal_context` — natural language description of when the relationship holds - `valid_from` — start date/time (if extractable) - `valid_to` — end date/time (if extractable) This enables **temporal queries** — asking about relationships at specific points in time. ::: {#temporal-config .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} WORKING_DIR_TEMP = Path("./_cache/06_advanced_features/temporal") WORKING_DIR_TEMP.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) rag_temp = GraphRAG( working_dir=str(WORKING_DIR_TEMP), enable_temporal_extraction=True, ) print(f"Temporal extraction: {rag_temp.enable_temporal_extraction}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Temporal extraction: True ``` ::: ::: ::: {#temporal-query-config .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} print("Temporal query parameters (QueryParam):") print() from nano_graphrag import QueryParam qp = QueryParam( time_range=("2023-01-01", "2024-01-01"), temporal_mode="any", ) print(f" time_range: {qp.time_range}") print(f" temporal_mode: {qp.temporal_mode}") print() print(" temporal_mode options:") print(" 'any' — match if any part of the relationship overlaps the time range") print(" 'all' — match only if the entire relationship is within the time range") print(" 'exact' — match only if valid_from and valid_to are both in range") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Temporal query parameters (QueryParam): time_range: ('2023-01-01', '2024-01-01') temporal_mode: any temporal_mode options: 'any' — match if any part of the relationship overlaps the time range 'all' — match only if the entire relationship is within the time range 'exact' — match only if valid_from and valid_to are both in range ``` ::: ::: Temporal extraction works with both the structured and legacy extraction backends. In structured mode, the Pydantic schema includes `temporal_context`, `valid_from`, and `valid_to` fields on relationships. ## 4. Community Reports Configuration Community reports are summaries generated for each cluster of entities. They power the **global query mode**. Key configuration options: ::: {#community-config .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} print("Community report configuration:") print() print("GraphRAG parameters:") print(" enable_community_reports=True # Generate reports (default: True)") print(" graph_cluster_algorithm='leiden' # Clustering algorithm ('leiden' or 'louvain')") print() print("QueryParam parameters for global search:") print(" global_min_community_rating=0 # Skip communities rated below this") print(" global_max_consider_community=512 # Max communities to consider") print(" global_max_token_for_community_report=16384 # Token budget for reports") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Community report configuration: GraphRAG parameters: enable_community_reports=True # Generate reports (default: True) graph_cluster_algorithm='leiden' # Clustering algorithm ('leiden' or 'louvain') QueryParam parameters for global search: global_min_community_rating=0 # Skip communities rated below this global_max_consider_community=512 # Max communities to consider global_max_token_for_community_report=16384 # Token budget for reports ``` ::: ::: ::: {#community-algo .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} WORKING_DIR_COMM = Path("./_cache/06_advanced_features/community") WORKING_DIR_COMM.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) rag_leiden = GraphRAG( working_dir=str(WORKING_DIR_COMM), graph_cluster_algorithm="leiden", ) rag_louvain = GraphRAG( working_dir=str(WORKING_DIR_COMM).replace("community", "community_louvain"), graph_cluster_algorithm="louvain", ) print(f"Default algorithm: {rag_leiden.graph_cluster_algorithm}") print(f"Alternative: {rag_louvain.graph_cluster_algorithm}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}

Recommended for most use cases. - **Louvain**: Faster, but may produce poorly disconnected communities. Good for large graphs where speed matters. ## 5. Graph Rebuild The `arebuild_graph()` method reconstructs the knowledge graph from stored extraction manifests — without re-running the LLM extraction. This is useful when: - You want to change the clustering algorithm - You want to re-generate community reports with different parameters - The graph was corrupted (e.g., due to a crash during insertion) ::: {#rebuild-demo .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} print("Graph rebuild example (not executed to save API calls):") print() print(" # Rebuild graph from stored manifests") print(" await rag.arebuild_graph()") print() print(" # This will:") print(" # 1. Read extraction manifests from document_index KV store") print(" # 2. Rebuild entity and relationship indexes") print(" # 3. Re-run community detection (Leiden/Louvain)") print(" # 4. Re-generate community reports via LLM") print(" #") print(" # Note: Community report generation still requires LLM calls,") print(" # but entity extraction is skipped (manifests are reused).") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Graph rebuild example (not executed to save API calls): # Rebuild graph from stored manifests await rag.arebuild_graph() # This will: # 1. Read extraction manifests from document_index KV store # 2. Rebuild entity and relationship indexes # 3. Re-run community detection (Leiden/Louvain) # 4. Re-generate community reports via LLM # # Note: Community report generation still requires LLM calls, # but entity extraction is skipped (manifests are reused). ``` ::: ::: The rebuild process leverages the `graph_contribution_index` KV store, which maps each entity and relationship to the documents that contributed to it. This index is built incrementally during insertion and can be fully reconstructed from the `document_index`. ## 6. Entity Registry nano-graphrag maintains an **EntityRegistry** that tracks canonical entity IDs and their aliases. This enables fuzzy entity resolution across documents. ::: {#entity-registry .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} import json from pathlib import Path registry_path = WORKING_DIR_INC / "entity_registry.json" if registry_path.exists(): with open(registry_path) as f: registry = json.load(f) entity_count = len(registry.get("entities", {})) alias_count = sum(len(e.get("aliases", [])) for e in registry.get("entities", {}).values()) print(f"Entity registry:") print(f" Canonical entities: {entity_count}") print(f" Total aliases: {alias_count}") else: print("Entity registry not yet created (run an insert first)") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Entity registry: Canonical entities: 3 Total aliases: 0 ``` ::: ::: The entity registry is stored at `{working_dir}/entity_registry.json` and supports: - **Exact resolution**: `registry.resolve_entity("Alice")` → canonical ID - **Fuzzy matching**: `registry.find_candidates("Alice Chen", threshold=0.9)` → candidates - **Alias tracking**: `"Alice Chen" → "Alice"` mapping ## 7. Feature Flags Summary ::: {#feature-flags-table .cell execution_count=14} ``` {.python .cell-code} features = [ ("enable_entity_linking", "False", "Merge duplicate entities across documents"), ("enable_temporal_extraction", "False", "Extract time-bound relationship fields"), ("enable_community_reports", "True", "Generate community summaries for global search"), ("enable_local", "True", "Enable entity-level vector search (local mode)"), ("enable_naive_rag", "False", "Enable chunk-level vector search (naive mode)"), ("enable_llm_cache", "True", "Cache LLM responses to avoid duplicate API calls"), ("enable_node_embedding", "False", "Compute node2vec embeddings for graph nodes"), ("structured_output", "True", "Use Pydantic JSON schema for extraction"), ("fallback_to_parsing", "True", "Retry with legacy parser on structured output failure"), ] print(f"{'Flag':<35s} {'Default':<10s} {'Description'}") print("-" * 100) for flag, default, desc in features: print(f"{flag:<35s} {default:<10s} {desc}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Flag Default Description ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- enable_entity_linking False Merge duplicate entities across documents enable_temporal_extraction False Extract time-bound relationship fields enable_community_reports True Generate community summaries for global search enable_local True Enable entity-level vector search (local mode) enable_naive_rag False Enable chunk-level vector search (naive mode) enable_llm_cache True Cache LLM responses to avoid duplicate API calls enable_node_embedding False Compute node2vec embeddings for graph nodes structured_output True Use Pydantic JSON schema for extraction fallback_to_parsing True Retry with legacy parser on structured output failure ``` ::: ::: ## Summary In this notebook we covered: - **Community reports** — Leiden vs Louvain clustering, rating filters, token budgets - **Graph rebuild** — reconstruct from manifests without re-extraction - **Entity registry** — canonical entity tracking with fuzzy alias resolution -
